title: Grafeo + flock + JSONL journal for decision memory
statement: Store decisions in an embedded Grafeo graph, serialised by flock, with an append-only JSONL journal as source of truth.
rationale: Grafeo is ~100x faster per call than FalkorDBLite and survives SIGKILL; both embedded engines silently lose concurrent writes so flock is mandatory; the journal makes the young v0.5.x engine a safe bet since rebuild replays it

title: Tag sets, not one project type
statement: Describe a project with a set of tags; rank precedent by tag overlap rather than exact type equality.
rationale: A single type forces a false choice — a service is backend AND java AND distributed, and which one a past decision rhymes with depends on the decision. Overlap gives a gradient instead of a binary, and small orthogonal tags get reused far more than compound names, so the vocabulary converges instead of drifting.

title: Derive project containment from the path key
statement: Treat each directory as its own project; derive monorepo containment from the absolute-path key rather than a stored parent edge.
rationale: Project.id is already an absolute path, so containment is a string-prefix fact that cannot go stale and needs no maintenance. Modules get their own tags so a Java backend and a Python bot in one repo never lend each other precedent, while root-level decisions (CI, branching, licensing) are inherited by every module.

title: Keep uv run + PEP 723, no durable venv
statement: Ship the CLI as a single PEP 723 file run via uv, rather than provisioning a persistent virtualenv.
rationale: Measured: uv run 72ms median vs venv 61ms — an 11ms difference, invisible inside agent turns that take 100s+. Both are dominated by ~50ms of importing grafeo, which a venv does not avoid. A venv would buy that 11ms in exchange for an install step where there is currently none, a environment to keep in sync, a staleness failure mode, and absolute interpreter paths in the hook and every command file.

title: Support Windows, not POSIX only
statement: precedent runs on Linux, macOS and Windows.
rationale: Distribution is aimed at other people, and a POSIX-only tool excludes a large share of them; the concrete cost was small (one dependency swap and one mechanism change) once measured.

title: The CLI shows, the model judges
statement: Deterministic string logic resolves exact lookups; deciding whether two different words mean the same thing is left to the model.
rationale: The difflib/subsequence drift guard was wrong on 7 of 11 realistic tag pairs (web-frontend vs web-backend, mobile-ios vs mobile-android) because SequenceMatcher scores a shared prefix and the thresholds were only ever tuned on suffix-sharing pairs; a guard that wrong trains the caller to reflex-bypass it, which is worse than no guard. See docs/adr/0001.

title: Identify a project by git remote, not by path
statement: A project's identity is its git remote plus a subpath; native paths become aliases collected on the node.
rationale: An absolute path makes one repo on two machines into two projects with no shared history, and made every Windows-recorded project report as dead on Linux; a home-relative id was rejected because it silently merges different projects that sit at the same relative path, and a wrong identity is worse than an absent one. See docs/adr/0002.

title: Use filelock rather than a hand-rolled cross-platform lock
statement: An existing cross-platform lock library, declared in the PEP 723 header.
rationale: fcntl imported at module level made the tool fail to start on Windows; hand-rolling the shim means owning a concurrency primitive on an OS we do not run and cannot test, and GrafeoDB/grafeo#405 (120 writes across 6 processes, 60 stored, no errors raised) is the local evidence for what a silently-wrong lock costs. See docs/adr/0003.

title: Relocate the store with a pointer file, not a symlink
statement: The store's real location lives in a file at the default path.
rationale: An env var cannot work because the SessionStart hook never sees one, and a symlink needs Developer Mode or elevation on Windows; a pointer file needs no privilege, no platform branch, and less code than the symlink handling it replaced. See docs/adr/0004.

title: Ship two manifests, generated from the ACR one
statement: agent-plugin.yaml is the source; the Claude Code plugin.json is generated from it.
rationale: Two hand-written manifests drift and drift means a Codex user silently gets last month's commands; generating downhill from the richer three-agent format fails loudly in CI on a schema change, where generating uphill ends with the missing fields hardcoded in the generator. See docs/adr/0005.
